Templates are complete, ready-made Tiptap editors for React. Each one is a real feature, not a bare editor: a comment thread, a document page, with the toolbar, menus and extensions already wired up. Pick a template, install it with the shadcn CLI, and change anything you like, because the code lands in your project.

<TemplateGallery />

## How templates work

Each template installs as a shadcn block: the CLI adds the template, the [editor](/docs/editor), and every component and extension it depends on. The template lands in its own folder, `components/templates/<name>/`, split into small files (types, constants, toolbar, panels and so on) with `index.tsx` as the entry point.

All templates store content as Tiptap JSON (`editor.getJSON()`) and display it with the [Static Renderer](/docs/static-renderer), which renders React elements instead of HTML. Content renders on the server, and stored content can't inject scripts. Use `generateHTML(json, extensions)` from `@tiptap/html` when you need HTML, for example in emails. It runs on the server as well as in the browser.

## Requirements

<Callout title="Templates use Tailwind CSS">
  The editor and static renderer ship plain CSS and work in any React app.
  Templates are styled with Tailwind CSS v4 and built on shadcn/ui components,
  so your project needs Tailwind and shadcn/ui. Run `npx shadcn@latest init`
  first if it isn't set up.
</Callout>

<Callout title="Already using Tiptap?">
  Tiptap packages must all be on the same version. The CLI installs the latest
  3.x, so if your project already has `@tiptap/*` packages on an older 3.x
  release, npm stops with an `ERESOLVE` peer dependency error. Update the
  packages you already have first, for example `npm install @tiptap/react@latest
  @tiptap/pm@latest @tiptap/starter-kit@latest`, then add the template.
</Callout>

Templates work with shadcn/ui built on either Radix UI or Base UI.

## FAQ

### Are the templates free?

Yes. Every template is MIT licensed and free to use in personal and commercial projects. There is no account, API key or Tiptap Pro subscription involved.

### Which Tiptap version do they use?

Tiptap v3. The templates use the open source Tiptap packages only (`@tiptap/react`, `@tiptap/starter-kit` and the free extensions).

### Do they work with Next.js?

Yes. The templates are client components, so they work in the Next.js App Router, Vite, Remix and any other React setup that runs shadcn/ui.

### How is this different from Tiptap's own templates?

Tiptap's templates install from the Tiptap CLI and use their own UI components. editorcn templates install with the shadcn CLI and are built from your existing shadcn/ui components and theme, so they match the rest of your app with no extra styling.
